ledger.note: 1613: Johor is taken. 'In 1612 he conquered Deli, and in 1613 Aru and Johor'; the page says Johor was 'taken in 1613 and later that year expelled the Acehnese garrison'.
1613: Johor expels the Acehnese garrison the same year. Johor was sacked again in 1623 ('again sacked Johor in 1623').

1617: Iskandar Muda conquers Pahang. 'In 1617 he conquered Pahang and carried its sultan Ahmed Syah to Aceh' (Aceh Sultanate page: 'once it conquered Pahang in 1617'). No garrison or end date is given.

1617: the page records the conquest and the sultan's removal, nothing about holding Pahang; closed the same year as a raid. Iskandar Thani, 'former prince of Pahang', later succeeded (Aceh Sultanate page). Re-checked 2026-10-19: the Taj ul-Alam page has Pahang lost during her reign (1641-1675), no year; the same-year close is still a bridge (confidence 1).

1619: Aceh takes Kedah. 'This conquest was followed by Kedah in 1619, in which the capital was laid waste'; a footnote gives 1620 (Ricklefs), and the Aceh Sultanate page puts Kedah in 1629, the year of the Malacca campaign.

1619: the page records a sack, not a lasting occupation; closed the same year. Re-checked 2026-10-19: no page opened gives the end of Kedah's subjection; the same-year close is still a bridge (confidence 1).

1620: Perak is captured. 'A similar capture of Perak occurred in 1620, when 5,000 people were captured and left to die in Aceh.' Held as a dependency until it defected to the Portuguese in 1629 (conflicts page).
1623: Iskandar Muda sacks Johor a second time. 'He again sacked Johor in 1623 and took Nias in 1624/5.' A sack, not a lasting hold; closed in the same year.
1623: the sack ends the same year; the page gives no garrison or occupation (bridged).
1624: Iskandar Muda takes Nias. 'took Nias in 1624/5.' Cliopatria draws Nias already in 1612.

1629: after the failed attack on Malacca, Perak defects to the Portuguese. 'Perak defects to the Portuguese', which the page treats as 'the turning point that ended Acehnese expansion'. Disagreement (2026-10-19): the Taj ul-Alam page says that in her reign (1641-1675) 'Aceh retained the tin-producing Perak', with Dutch killed in Perak in 1651 and a VOC treaty in 1659, so the tie may have outlasted 1629; no page gives its end. Confidence lowered to 1; the Perak dossier should settle it.

ledger.note: 1641: after Iskandar Thani (d. 15 February 1641) Nias, Simeulue and the highlands slip away. 'The reign of Taj ul-Alam saw a contraction of the sultanate's power outside the Acehnese heartland' (reign 18 February 1641 to 23 October 1675); the Aceh Sultanate page: 'Aceh's control weakened while regional rulers gained effective power' and, in the 1680s, 'every corner shelters a separate king or governor'. No page names a successor state, so the counterpart is 'nobody'; the year and the land are Cliopatria's 1640 homeland, moved one year later.

ledger.note: 1666: the VOC expels Aceh from the west coast of Sumatra. 'expelling the Sultanate of Aceh from the coast of West Sumatra in 1666' after the Minang revolted against the Aceh governors around 1665; the VOC wrote on 9 October 1668 that it 'had taken control of the west coast'.
1666: Pagaruyung escapes Aceh. 'Aceh's influence on Pagaruyung then weakened' once the VOC drove Aceh from the coast.

ledger.note: 1669: Deli falls away. 'On the east coast, Deli fell away from Acehnese rule in 1669.' The Alauddin al-Kahar page uses Deli as the later name of the Aru kingdom, so the loss is read as the Deli-Aru coast of the 1612-1613 gains; the year is the page's, the extent the researcher's reading.

1873: the Dutch attack Aceh. 'An expedition under Major General Johan Harmen Rudolf Köhler was sent out on 26 March 1873' and 'was able to occupy most of the coastal areas by April' (the war follows the 1871 Sumatra Treaty). The zone is the whole sultanate: the Dutch declared it annexed after the capital fell in 1874, but resistance held the interior until 1904.

January 1874: the Dutch take the dalam and Sultan Mahmud Syah abandons Banda Aceh. 'By January 1874, deteriorating conditions forced Sultan Mahmud Syah and his followers to abandon Banda Aceh'; the court sits at Pagar Ayer from 1875 (Aceh Sultanate page).
1878: the court moves to Indrapuri (Aceh Sultanate page: Pagar Ayer 1875-1878, Indrapuri 1878-1879).
1879: the court moves to Keumala (Keumala 1879-1898).
1898: the court leaves Keumala for Kuta Sawang and then Batee Illiek-Samalanga as van Heutsz, 'proclaimed governor of Aceh' in 1898, presses in (Aceh War page).
1901: the court moves to Loyang Sekam-Laut (1901-1903).
1904: the war ends in Dutch victory. 'In 1904, the Sultanate of Aceh surrendered, though guerilla resistance would continue for some time after'; the sultan had capitulated in 1903.

1904: Aceh passes to the Dutch East Indies. 'By the end of 1904 most of Aceh was under Dutch control'; the Dutch had declared the sultanate abolished and Aceh annexed after taking the capital in 1874, but 'did not establish wider control of its territory until after 1908' (Aceh page).
1904: the Aceh Sultanate ends. Infobox: 'The dissolution of the Aceh Sultanate by the Dutch: 1904'; the sultan Muhammad Da'ud Syah II surrendered in 1903.

wars.name: Acehnese-Portuguese conflicts

zones.text: Samudera Pasai (north-east Aceh coast around Lhokseumawe)

wars.outcome: Aceh took Pedir (1522) and Pasai (1523-1524) from the Portuguese orbit, besieged Malacca repeatedly (1537, 1547, 1568, 1573, 1575, 1582, 1615, 1629) without taking it, and its great 1629 attack failed.
wars.note: Zones are the land that changed hands; the Malacca sieges moved no border. Johor sided with the Portuguese in 1568 and 1577 and was attacked by Aceh in 1582 and 1615.

wars.name: Iskandar Muda's conquests in Sumatra and the Malay Peninsula
wars.outcome: Deli (1612), Aru and Johor (1613), Pahang (1617), Kedah (1619/20), Perak (1620) and Nias (1624/5); the peninsular conquests were sacks and captive-taking that did not outlast 1629.
wars.note: The Aceh Sultanate page puts Kedah in 1629; the Iskandar Muda page in 1619 with a footnote for 1620.

wars.outcome: The VOC arrived at Padang in 1663; the Minang revolted against the Aceh governors around 1665; in 1666 the VOC drove Aceh from the coast.
wars.note: The page's dates: first arrival of the VOC 1663, rebellion 'around 1665', expulsion 1666. The Taj ul-Alam page has the Dutch expelling the Acehnese 'in 1664' and the Pariaman page a Dutch treaty with Aceh in 1663 (formal control); the dossier keeps the Pagaruyung page's 1666.

wars.name: Aceh War
wars.outcome: Dutch victory: the capital fell in January 1874, the Dutch withdrew behind a fortified line around Banda Aceh in 1884, van Heutsz and Colijn conquered most of Aceh from 1898, the sultan capitulated in 1903 and the sultanate surrendered in 1904.
wars.note: The Anglo-Dutch Sumatra Treaty of 2 November 1871 'established full Dutch influence over the Aceh Sultanate' (Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1871 page, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anglo-Dutch_Treaty_of_1871); the colonial government declared the war over on 13 October 1880, and the Gayo remained a centre of resistance to 1914.

certainty.note: The Sumatran uplands, the east-coast lands and the west-coast governors' reach are approximate; no treaty fixes any frontier.

The homeland is a coast-and-valley realm of semi-autonomous uleebalang; the Dutch and British treaties (1871) fixed spheres, not lines. The Dutch lines of 1884 around Banda Aceh are a military line, not a border.

notes: Cliopatria 'Sultanate of Aceh' (16 shapes, 1516..1959). (1) The sultanate ends in 1904 (surrender; infobox dissolution), not 1913 or 1959: the five shapes 1946..1959 are verdict wrong (Aceh inside the Republic of Indonesia; the 1953-1959 shapes coincide with Daud Beureu'eh's Darul Islam rebellion, for which another group could write a rebel dossier 'Aceh Darul Islam', 1953-1959). (2) Cliopatria adds Pedir and Pasai in 1529, though the pages date them 1522 and 1524; new keyframes 1514, 1522, 1524 and an adjusted 1526 carry the correction. (3) The 1609-1639 west-coast strip runs to -2.9 S, beyond what the Iskandar Muda page allows (Aceh never reached Inderapura); trimmed by a 110 km disc whose centre is the researcher's coordinates. (4) Cliopatria drops the west coast, the east coast and Nias in 1640; the dossier keeps the 1626 extent for 1640, drops Nias, Simeulue and the highlands in 1641 (confidence 1; 'contraction outside the heartland' in Taj ul-Alam's reign), the west coast in 1666 (VOC; pages differ: 1663, 1664, 1666) and the east coast (Deli and Aru) in 1669 (Taj ul-Alam page). (5) The Aceh Sultanate page's infobox is inconsistent: Founded 1480, capital from 1496, Pedir vassal 1497-1514, reign list from c.1514; the dossier starts in 1514. The infobox also says 'Protectorate of the Ottoman Empire (1569-1903)'; this is a nominal tie that belongs to an Ottoman dossier and is not drawn here. (6) Peninsular conquests (Johor 1613, Pahang 1617, Kedah 1619/20, Perak 1620) are in no Cliopatria shape; they are carried as one-year occupations/contests (Johor, Pahang, Kedah) and a vassalage (Perak 1620-1629); the pages give no garrison dates, so the spans are the researcher's bridging (confidence 1 on the ends). (7) The Aceh page gives no area; no area comparison was possible beyond Cliopatria's own figures. (8) The later capitals' coordinates (Pagar Ayer, Indrapuri, Keumala, Kuta Sawang, Batee Illiek-Samalanga, Loyang Sekam-Laut) are approximate readings; the page gives names and years only; the gazetteer lacks them. (9) Cliopatria's Aceh neighbours list shows 'Qajar Dynasty 1895-1897' beside Aceh, a Cliopatria artefact; the Dutch East Indies has no shape touching Aceh in those years. Counterparts needing dossiers: Sultanate of Pedir, Pahang Sultanate, Deli, Aru (Kingdom of Aru), Pagaruyung Kingdom (se-02-x), Samudera Pasai (exists). The fetch tool returns a model summary of each page, so quotation marks mean 'as the fetched text gave it'. REPAIR 2026-10-19 (after the adversarial review): (a) Aru is now drawn from 1613 (new keyframe sultanate-of-aceh_1613 and the 1624 keyframe), and the 1612 verdict is valid for 1612 only; the Aru region is Cliopatria's own 1626 step (60 cells) instead of the 90 km disc, which held 31 inland cells that Cliopatria never draws. (b) The 1641 loss now has counterpart 'nobody' and its own keyframe; Deli's fall in 1669 comes from the Taj ul-Alam page. (c) The Mentawai Islands (15 cells) are cut from every keyframe from 1612; Simeulue and Langkat stay, marked unverified: page budget. (d) 1540 gain moved to 1539 (Batak war, Alauddin al-Kahar page). (e) A second sack of Johor in 1623 is recorded as a one-year contest. (f) Perak's vassal_end (1629) is lowered to confidence 1 because the Taj ul-Alam page says Aceh retained Perak in 1641-1675. NOT DONE: the Ottoman protectorate of the infobox (1569-1903) is left out on purpose: the Ottoman expedition page opened has no 1569 and calls it an 'informal alliance' and a nineteenth-century Achenese claim of dependency.
